context: Adults receiving IV fluid therapy in hospital
trigger_summary: An adult receiving IV fluids in hospital requires fluid and electrolyte assessment or review.
required_inputs: History; current medicines; fluid status; NEWS/vital signs; fluid balance; weight; urea, creatinine and electrolytes.
management_output: Assess and manage fluid and electrolyte needs at every ward review. Keep a 24-hour fluid and electrolyte prescription and monitoring plan, reviewed daily by an expert initially.
limitations: Applies only within the adult hospital IV-fluid scope of CG174 and does not provide a condition-specific treatment pathway.

context: During or within 24 hours of IV-fluid therapy
trigger_summary: Sodium <130 mmol/L, no other likely cause, and temporally related to IV-fluid therapy.
required_inputs: Sodium; baseline sodium; IV-fluid type/volume; timing; fluid status; renal function; alternative causes.
management_output: Reassess the IV-fluid management plan and adjust the prescription for the sodium deficit or excess. Seek expert help for a complex imbalance and report a clear IV-fluid mismanagement incident through the standard critical-incident process.
limitations: No definitive sodium-correction regimen is provided by CG174.

context: During or within 24 hours of IV-fluid therapy
trigger_summary: Sodium >=155 mmol/L, baseline normal/low, IV regimen included 0.9% sodium chloride, and no other likely cause.
required_inputs: Sodium; baseline sodium; IV-fluid composition; timing; fluid status; renal function; alternative causes.
management_output: Reassess the IV-fluid management plan and adjust the prescription for the sodium deficit or excess. Seek expert help for the imbalance and report a clear IV-fluid mismanagement incident through the standard critical-incident process.
limitations: No definitive sodium-correction regimen is provided by CG174.

context: During or within 24 hours of IV-fluid therapy
trigger_summary: Potassium <3.0 mmol/L, likely related to IV fluids without adequate potassium provision, and no other obvious cause.
required_inputs: Potassium; baseline potassium; IV-fluid prescription; timing; renal function; medicines; other potassium losses.
management_output: Reassess and adjust the IV-fluid and electrolyte prescription, then continue monitoring. Do not add potassium to IV-fluid bags. Report a clear IV-fluid mismanagement incident through the standard critical-incident process.

context: During or within 24 hours of IV-fluid therapy
trigger_summary: Potassium >5.5 mmol/L with no other obvious cause and temporal relation to IV-fluid therapy.
required_inputs: Potassium; baseline potassium; IV-fluid prescription; timing; renal function; medicines; alternative causes.
management_output: Reassess the IV-fluid management plan and adjust the prescription for the electrolyte excess. Review contributing factors, continue monitoring, and report a clear IV-fluid mismanagement incident through the standard critical-incident process.
limitations: Not a complete acute hyperkalaemia treatment pathway.

context: Adult with CKD starting or increasing a renin-angiotensin system antagonist
trigger_summary: An adult with CKD is starting a renin-angiotensin system antagonist or has a dose increase.
required_inputs: CKD status; eGFR; serum potassium; medicine and dose-change date.
management_output: Measure serum potassium and eGFR before treatment and repeat both between 1 and 2 weeks after starting treatment and after every dose increase. More frequent potassium monitoring may be needed with other medicines that promote hyperkalaemia.
limitations: This schedule applies to adults with CKD using a renin-angiotensin system antagonist; additional monitoring remains a clinical decision.

context: Adult with CKD before a renin-angiotensin system antagonist
required_inputs: CKD status; pretreatment potassium; planned medicine.
management_output: Do not routinely offer the renin-angiotensin system antagonist. If hyperkalaemia prevents its use, assess and treat other factors that promote hyperkalaemia and recheck serum potassium.
limitations: Final prescribing decision remains with the responsible clinician.

context: Adult with CKD taking a renin-angiotensin system antagonist
trigger_summary: Potassium >=6.0 mmol/L after other medicines known to promote hyperkalaemia have been discontinued.
required_inputs: CKD status; potassium; current RAAS antagonist; other hyperkalaemia-promoting medicines and their status.
management_output: Stop the renin-angiotensin system antagonist when serum potassium is 6.0 mmol/L or above after other medicines known to promote hyperkalaemia have been discontinued.
limitations: Must verify contributing medicines and the complete clinical context.

context: Adult with CKD stage 3b-5 or heart failure, not on dialysis
trigger_summary: Confirmed potassium >=5.5 mmol/L; an optimised RAAS-inhibitor dosage is not being taken because of hyperkalaemia; patient is not on dialysis.
required_inputs: Confirmed potassium; CKD stage or heart failure; RAAS-inhibitor optimisation status; dialysis status.
management_output: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate is a NICE option when all stated eligibility conditions are confirmed.
limitations: Does not select a dose or replace standard emergency care.

context: Adult with CKD stage 3b-5 or heart failure, not on dialysis
trigger_summary: Confirmed potassium >=6.0 mmol/L; RAAS inhibitor is absent or reduced because of hyperkalaemia; patient is not on dialysis.
required_inputs: Confirmed potassium; CKD stage or heart failure; RAAS-inhibitor status; dialysis status.
management_output: Patiromer and sodium zirconium cyclosilicate are NICE options when all stated eligibility conditions are confirmed.
limitations: This is an eligibility result, not a medicine selection or dosing instruction. It does not replace standard emergency care.

context: Adult in emergency care receiving standard emergency care
trigger_summary: Acute life-threatening hyperkalaemia and emergency-care setting are clinically confirmed, with standard care underway.
required_inputs: Acute life-threatening classification; emergency-care setting; confirmation that standard emergency care is underway.
management_output: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate or patiromer may be used as a NICE option for acute life-threatening hyperkalaemia only alongside standard care in emergency care.
limitations: This eligibility result does not define or replace standard emergency care, select a medicine, or provide a dose.

context: Acute kidney injury with hyperkalaemia not responding to medical management
trigger_summary: AKI, hyperkalaemia and failure to respond to medical management.
required_inputs: AKI status; potassium trend; treatments already given; clinical condition; ECG/complications; fluid status.
management_output: Refer immediately for renal replacement therapy and involve nephrology and/or critical care. Base the decision to start therapy on the whole clinical condition, not an isolated potassium value.
limitations: The decision must be based on the whole clinical condition, not an isolated potassium value.

trigger_summary: Possible primary hyperparathyroidism with albumin-adjusted serum calcium >=2.60 mmol/L.
required_inputs: Albumin-adjusted calcium; symptoms; fracture/osteoporosis history; renal stones; suspected PHPT.
management_output: Repeat albumin-adjusted serum calcium at least once. If it is 2.60 mmol/L or above on at least 2 occasions, measure PTH using a random sample with a concurrent albumin-adjusted calcium measurement. Do not use ionised calcium for this diagnostic pathway.
limitations: This is a diagnostic PHPT pathway, not acute general hypercalcaemia management. The engine does not infer a second calcium result or PTH result.

trigger_summary: Symptoms of hypercalcaemia, end-organ disease, or adjusted calcium >=2.85 mmol/L.
required_inputs: Confirmed PHPT; adjusted calcium; symptoms; renal stones; fragility fracture or osteoporosis.
management_output: Refer to a surgeon with expertise in parathyroid surgery when one or more stated NICE criteria are present.
limitations: Applies only to confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism.

context: Confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism without a mandatory referral criterion
trigger_summary: Primary hyperparathyroidism is confirmed but no criterion in recommendation 1.3.1 is confirmed.
required_inputs: Confirmed PHPT; adjusted calcium; symptoms; renal stones; fragility fracture or osteoporosis; end-organ disease.
management_output: Consider referral to a surgeon with expertise in parathyroid surgery even though none of the mandatory referral features in recommendation 1.3.1 is confirmed.
limitations: Applies only to confirmed primary hyperparathyroidism and is a consider recommendation, not an automatic referral instruction.

trigger_summary: Persistent hyponatraemia despite the maximum fludrocortisone dose.
required_inputs: Confirmed primary adrenal insufficiency; sodium trend; fludrocortisone dose/status; specialist involvement.
management_output: Consider sodium chloride supplementation according to specialist endocrinology advice.
limitations: Applies only to primary adrenal insufficiency.

context: No applicable NICE recommendation in the approved catalogue
trigger_summary: The condition or clinical context does not match a NICE-supported rule.
required_inputs: Condition; context; existing local protocol; specialist availability.
management_output: Do not generate treatment instructions. Display that an approved local protocol or specialist review is required.
limitations: This is a safety rule, not a treatment recommendation.
